CIRCUIT: a six-transistor discrete network on a single sheet, fed by five one-port DC rails drawn as up-arrows (+15V #0 at (584,72), +10V #2 at (320,187), +6V #5 at (597,301), +5V #13 at (920,495), +3V #15 at (123,477)) and returned to a single GND #29 at (823,882) on the bottom rail. Transistors: Q3 NPN (803,289) top right, Q10 PNP (358,433) upper left, Q14 NPN (586,524) centre, Q16 PNP (189,518) left, Q23 PNP (683,656) drawn on its side (base bar horizontal, base lead up), Q25 NPN (358,716) lower left. 30 components, 20 nets.

JUDGEMENT CALLS AND SITE DECISIONS
  S42 (604,729) - CROSSING, and it is unambiguous: the drafter drew a full semicircular hop, the horizontal wire arcing up over the x~604 column between x=576 and x=628 (hop score 36.8). This is the sheet's one and only crossing, and it is the proof that this drafter marks no-connects with a hop. Reading it as a junction would short Q25's collector / R19's bottom onto the R21-bottom node, i.e. it would put R21's bottom, Q23's emitter and the ground rail all on the same net as ... which they already are, so the visible consequence is small, but the arc is drawn and must be honoured.
  Every other site with degree >= 3 on this sheet is a plain T - one wire physically ending on another - and every one was called junction. The CRITICAL ones, each checked in its own 5x crop: S1 (585,119) +15V lead onto the top rail; S5 (376,214) +10V lead onto the R1/R4 column, with a large solder dot; S12 (381,348) R8 branch onto the R4/Q10 column; S13 (596,357) the +6V column meeting the y~357 crossbar, drawn with an unmistakable fat solder blob (dot 2.7) - degree 4 but a dotted junction, not a crossing; S14 (725,358) the crossbar ending on the D6/D9 column; S18 (823,455) the y~453 crossbar onto the x~826 column; S19 (774,455) the R18 drop onto the y~453 crossbar; S24 (369,513) R17 onto the Q10-collector column; S25 (127,516) the Q16 base wire onto the +3V column; S26 (829,531) the +5V lead onto the x~826 column, again with a fat dot; S35 (371,640) R19-bottom / Q25-collector / the long ground wire, with a fat dot; S36 (603,665) Q23's emitter lead onto the x~604 column; S41 (191,697) R27 onto the Q16-collector column; S45 (196,822), S46 (359,823), S47 (604,829), S48 (769,830), S49 (827,830) - the five drops landing on the bottom rail.
  Non-critical sites S0, S3, S4, S7, S9, S11, S15, S16, S20, S21, S23, S27, S28, S29, S32, S39, S40 are all handwritten value labels ('50KOhm', '30KOhm', '150 KOhm', '100 KOhm', '70KOhm', '+6 V', '+5 V', '+15V') touching a wire or a symbol; they were left at their defaults because they contain no terminal. Note S16 (253,398) carries hop=67.2 - that is the curl of the '0' in '30KOhm', not a real hop. 24 gap bridges were found and none of them changes the netlist; none was dropped.

MERGE (1) - ["24.1","29.0"], i.e. R24's bottom terminal is on net 0.
  This is the one place where the tracer's graph is wrong, and it is a bounding-box artefact rather than an ink question. R24 (769,727) has its bbox at x 752..786, y 701..753. Three things meet at (767,754), one pixel below the bbox: R24's own bottom lead, the long horizontal wire arriving from the left at y~753, and the drop that continues down x~769 to the bottom rail at S48 (769,830). inkmap 24px at (768,752) shows the join explicitly - row 754 has ink at x=764..766 and row 755 has ink at x=765..770, so the horizontal's right end and the vertical's top share pixels at (765..766, 755) and are 4-connected. But the box mask cut the horizontal off at (748,753) (edge e101) and the drop at (765,756) (edge e102), so the tracer saw two unrelated ports (R24 p0 'L' and p1 'B') and kept the horizontal's net separate from ground.
  Consequence: the long wire that leaves S35 (371,640) at R19's bottom, runs right to (435,648), drops to y~750, HOPS over the x~604 column at S42 and ends on R24's bottom lead is the ground return for R19's bottom and Q25's collector. Merging is what the drawing says, and it also explains the routing: R19-bottom needs to reach ground, and the nearest point of the ground net is R24's bottom lead, so the router went there instead of down to the rail. Without the merge, R19.1 / R24.1 / Q25.0 sit on a private 3-terminal net and Q25's collector floats relative to ground - which contradicts the ink.

MANUAL NET n20 - R11 bottom and Q14 collector.
  Same class of problem, worse: R11's bbox (x 580..614, y 418..474) and Q14's bbox (x 553..619, y 480..568) are only 6 px apart, and the wire that joins R11's bottom lead to Q14's upper (collector) lead lives entirely inside that 6 px gap. The tracer therefore found NO port at all on R11's bottom edge (its p1/p2 are strokes of the '60 kOhm' label) and only 2 of Q14's 3 leads (left = base, bottom = emitter). edges.py at (600,480) radius 40 returns a single edge, e41, which is label ink. A zoom at 6x makes the connection obvious: the 60k zigzag ends at (595,470), the lead continues down to (600,487) and merges into Q14's collector lead, which slopes down-left to the base bar at (574,500).
  Since neither terminal has a usable port, `merge` cannot express this (it only unions terminals already in the map), so I used `ports` to null out R11.t1 (it was pointing at label ink and produced the 1-terminal net n10 in the tracer's output) and `manual_nets` to place R11.t1 and Q14.t0 on a shared new net 'n20'. Nothing else touches that node, so it is a legitimate private 2-terminal net. 'n20' does not collide: the automatic labeller only allocated n1..n18 here.

PIN ORDER - four transistors needed work. The rule I used: whichever lead carries the arrowhead is the EMITTER, regardless of which way the barb points, and the odd lead touching the base bar broadside is the BASE.
  #10 BJT-PNP (358,433): the barb sits on the UPPER lead, at about (357..367, 398..414) on the run from the base bar (340,417) to (383,380); the lower lead (176,540)->(370,484) is bare. So emitter = upper p0 (383,380), collector = lower p1 (370,484). ports {"0":1,"2":0}. Result t0=n8 (down to R17/R19), t1=n9 (base, R12), t2=n5 (up to R4).
  #16 BJT-PNP (189,518): barb on the UPPER lead near (188..196, 481..495); lower lead bare. emitter = upper p1 (209,467), collector = lower p0 (193,568). ports {"0":0,"2":1}. Result t0=n14 (bottom rail), t1=n13 (+3V), t2=n10 (R12).
  #23 BJT-PNP (683,656), drawn rotated 90 degrees: base bar is the HORIZONTAL stroke y~645 from x=655 to x=703, base lead goes up at x=683; the two other leads leave the bar down-left and down-right. At 12x the solid barb is unmistakably on the DOWN-LEFT lead, filling (652..669, 648..660), with the down-right lead completely clean. emitter = left p1 (638,665), collector = right p0 (728,669). ports {"0":0,"2":1}. Result t0=n17 (R24 top), t1=n15 (R18/base), t2=0 (the x~604 column to the ground rail).
  #14 BJT-NPN (586,524): the tracer had t0 pointing at the BASE lead and t1 at the emitter, with t2 unresolved. Barb is on the lower-right lead (about (590..600, 547..562)), so emitter = bottom p1 (600,571); base = left p0 (550,514); collector = the upper lead, which has no port (see MANUAL NET). ports {"0":null,"1":0,"2":1}.
  #3 BJT-NPN (803,289) and #25 BJT-NPN (358,716) were already right and were re-checked: in both the barb is on the lower lead (emitter) and the collector is the upper lead - #3 t0=n1 (top rail) / t1=n3 (base) / t2=n4 (+5V column); #25 t0=0 (collector, up to R19 and the ground wire) / t1=n18 (base, R27) / t2=n14 (emitter, bottom rail).

CLASSES: all 30 accepted. One reservation worth recording: #23 is labelled BJT-PNP and I kept it, but its emitter barb points AWAY from the base bar (down-left), which is the NPN convention, whereas #10 and #16 - also PNP - have barbs pointing INTO the base bar. So either the drafter was inconsistent on this one symbol or the COCO class is wrong. It does not change the netlist: the arrow identifies the emitter either way, and that is all the terminal order depends on. Everything else (three diodes #6/#9/#26 plus #7, twelve resistors, five one-port V-DC arrows, one GND) matches the drawing.

UNRESOLVED: nothing. Every terminal has a net, every net has at least two terminals, ERC is clean, and no component is marked unconnected.
